name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.25.0 (released 2026-06-24, https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/tag/v2.25.0) adds password reset via emailed magic links and reworks email verification to use durable, single-use expiring links instead of in-memory 6-digit codes. v2.24.0 introduced an opt-in in-memory ACL cache (`auth-access-cache`) to reduce database load and fixed a critical case-insensitive ACL topic matching bug on SQLite. Recent releases also addressed several security issues including an SSRF via web push endpoint regex, a file preview XSS via crafted SVGs, and a switch to cryptographically secure RNG for tokens. The project is actively maintained with frequent releases and community contributions.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL 2.0 (client) — check repository for exact dual-license details
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2025/2026 with active community contributions
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — token-based auth, ACL per topic, email verification, password reset, and an opt-in in-memory ACL cache
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud instance

breaking_excerpts: Email verification reworked from in-memory 6-digit codes to durable, single-use, expiring magic links — existing in-flight verification codes will no longer work after upgrade

Fix case-insensitive ACL topic matching on SQLite: access control rules now correctly match only exact-case topics (e.g., rule for 'secret' no longer matches 'SECRET') — may affect existing ACL configurations relying on case-insensitive matching
smtp-sender-verify flag now required to send email notifications on ntfy.sh; unverified email addresses are rejected

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise supports a massive number of notification services through a unified API, but is a library/CLI tool rather than a persistent pub-sub server with topic subscriptions.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet offers cross-device notification mirroring and file sharing, but the free tier is limited and it is a closed-source cloud service with no self-hosting option.

alternatives.name: Ntopng Alerts / Mosquitto (MQTT)
alternatives.review: Eclipse Mosquitto is a lightweight open-source MQTT broker suited for IoT pub-sub messaging, but requires MQTT client libraries and lacks native HTTP push or mobile notification delivery.
